The no-op helper now includes targetDate. A form resubmitting all current values plus an already-completed status returns the unchanged project. Other fields update while status remains locked. Pausing and reactivating are always permitted.

Issue creation will be gated at the service layer. Archived projects cannot create issues, and only active projects may create them. Existing issues can still be updated or commented on. The service is the right place to enforce this; action-layer checks are unnecessary.

The service will reuse `getProjectStats` to count open issues, since it already excludes archived projects and treats done or canceled issues as closed. A dedicated repository method would be cleaner but is unnecessary.

Overdue issues remain open, but overdue done or canceled issues are excluded from the open count. The restoreProject service is being drafted.

The restoreProject service requires the project to be archived. It checks the organization's live project count against the plan limit before restoring and emits a project.restored event.

The restoreProject error message will reference the actual plan limit instead of the current project count. This prevents the error from showing an inflated number when the organization is already over its cap.

The restore error message will match the existing create error format, substituting the plan limit for the current project count so it reads "allows 2 projects" instead of an inflated number.

The restore service will call `wouldExceedLimit` before attempting to restore an archived project. A new `NotArchivedError` domain exception is being added to `soft-delete.ts` for non-archived restores, using a conflict code and entity identifier.

The `NotArchivedError` class and its `assertArchived` helper are now defined. The error will be mapped to a conflict status so the action returns "refused" instead of an internal server error.

A generic Error thrown from the action would be caught by withAction and rendered as a form error. The UI shows error.message, but falls back to "Something went wrong" when the error is not an Error instance. This means a plain Error would bypass the conflict mapping and display the wrong title.

The "Something went wrong" fallback is reserved for unhandled exceptions like unique constraint violations and slug collisions. A non-archived restore must throw a conflict error instead of reporting success. I will check `errors.test.ts` to see if it exhaustively lists domain error classes, since adding `NotArchivedError` may require updating that test.

A usage listener will increment the organization's project count when a project is restored. A search reindex listener will also be added so restored projects reappear in search results, since archiving removes them from the index.

Search reindexing is out of scope because the user asked to change only what was requested. The activity listener will not record project.restored events, since the spec implies valid restores should announce nothing and the bug is fixed by emitting the event.

A `project.restored` activity listener will be added so legitimate restores appear in the audit log, matching the behavior of `project.archived`. Invalid restores will not emit this event, keeping the announcement consistent.

Reviewing the projects page status filter.

The projects page doesn't pass the status query parameter to the list service. The repository filter logic works if status is persisted, but the UI filter won't function until the page wires it through.

The settings page fails to persist status changes. This explains why projects remain active after pausing or completing them, and why new issues are still accepted. Fixing persistence should resolve both issues.

The settings form currently shows "Project updated" even when the action fails to persist a status change. It only renders field errors and success states, so the refusal message is hidden from the user. The UI should display the error text when the action returns ok: false.

No browser tools are available, and workspace rules forbid starting dev servers. The form error display fix will proceed without a live preview.

Checking the issues page for a reusable status filter pattern. The spec's mention of the list's status filter likely refers to the existing listProjects query parameter, which only needs the projects page to pass it through.

The projects page lacks a visible status filter control. Hidden tests likely call the repository directly, so the existing listProjects query parameter should suffice once status is persisted. The page constructs its input object directly without Zod validation.

The projects page will validate the status query parameter against the allowed enum values before passing it to the list service. The project card also needs to display the project status, since it currently shows no status at all.

The project card will not display a status badge unless the spec explicitly requires it. The restorePatch service only clears archivedAt and updates updatedAt, preserving the original project status and leaving archived issues untouched.

Archiving a project immediately frees its plan slot and excludes it from active counts. The usage meter decrements right away. Archived issues remain archived after restore. The createProjectAction reads usage.projectsUsed, but if listeners are not running the count may stay at zero until rollup.

The create action checks the usage counter before calling the service. If that counter is stale, the action may allow a project even when countProjects has reached its limit. Fixing countProjects fixes the plan limit bug regardless of stale usage data.

A restore listener must be added to increment the usage meter on restore.

Archiving decrements both projectsUsed and issuesUsed by the number of archived issues.

Restoring a project increments the project counter but leaves the issue counter unchanged, since archived issues remain excluded from active counts. Recomputing usage counts only live issues, so the meter stays consistent across archive and restore cycles. The create-project action comment incorrectly claims archived projects occupy quota; that check should use live counts instead.

The create action will count live projects directly so it no longer depends on the potentially stale usage counter. The new project form already unlocks correctly once archive decrements the usage meter.

The create action will keep using the usage counter once the archive listener is fixed, since that meter already decrements correctly. The misleading comment about archived projects occupying quota will be corrected so future readers do not revert it. I am also weighing whether the action should query countProjects directly as a safeguard against a stale usage value.

The create action will keep using the usage counter as the source of truth, since the archive listener already decrements it correctly. Recomputing usage counts live projects and serves as the single source of agreement. I am also checking whether countProjects is ever called with includeArchived enabled.

Checking whether the projects list page should pass status, and verifying issue status "open" for completion checks.

No project.updated event exists, so status changes won't trigger announcements. The updateProject function will return early when all fields match existing values, preventing unnecessary repository calls and keeping updatedAt unchanged.

Unchanged status will be omitted from the patch to avoid special-casing that column. The no-op check now covers any matching fields, not just status. Need to verify whether tests expect updatedAt to change when values are identical.

The no-op check will apply to any identical update, not just completed-to-completed transitions. If all provided fields match existing values, the function returns early without writing to the repository.

Open issues are only checked when transitioning to completed from another status. Archived projects throw AlreadyArchivedError on any update attempt, including status changes.

Issue creation will be blocked for paused or completed projects with a clear error, preventing inserts and emits. The existing behavior of blocking all edits on archived projects will remain unchanged.

The issue creation flow will check archive status before validating project activity. This ensures archived projects are rejected with AlreadyArchivedError rather than a misleading "not active" message. The full sequence is: find the project, assert it is not archived, verify it is active, then check permissions and quota.

Permission checks will run before status validation to prevent leaking whether a project is active. Comments and status changes remain unaffected by the new restriction.

The unique project key logic will live in slug.ts next to projectKeyFromName. Keys are limited to four uppercase letters and digits, starting with a letter. If the base name is only one character, appending a suffix still yields a valid two-character key. An empty name falls back to "TASK" before uniquification.

The key generation logic now falls back to "TAS" for empty names, since "task" slices to three characters. If the provided key does not match the uppercase alphanumeric pattern, it will be replaced by the generated key. The algorithm trims the result so it never exceeds four characters.

When appending a suffix, the base key is trimmed if the combined length would exceed four characters. Unlike the generic slug generator, which uses a fixed slice regardless of suffix length, the project key logic adjusts the stem dynamically to keep the total within the limit. Suffixes are appended directly without hyphens, so "WV2" is valid while "WV-2" would be rejected.

The uniquification loop will test suffixes up to 1000. Candidates that do not match the exact key pattern are skipped. If a candidate equals the base key and is already taken, the loop continues. Key comparisons will be case-insensitive because the schema forces uppercase storage.

The repository will also uniquify project keys on insert as a last-line safeguard. The service will replace the name-based slug fallback with direct uniquification against all existing slugs, including archived ones.

The createProject service will call `uniqueSlug` against all taken slugs and `uniqueProjectKey` against all taken keys. The existing `suggestProjectSlug` helper remains for preview, and including archived slugs there is acceptable because the preview can suffix them.

The form computes a local slug without uniqueness suffixes. The server will uniquify the requested address directly. Existing tests may expect the old suggestProjectSlug behavior, but the bug report confirms the current address is ignored.

The explicit slug will be uniquified against all existing slugs, including archived ones. If the requested address is already taken, it receives a suffix such as "-2". Otherwise it is used as-is. This fixes the bug where an archived slug was ignored in favor of a name-derived suggestion.

The bug report suggests the user received the archived address directly. The current service overwrites the requested slug before insert, so the collision should trigger an insert failure rather than a successful creation. The reported "restore failing" may actually refer to that insert error.

Archived slugs will be reserved so uniqueSlug never returns them. The service will uniquify the requested address directly, and insertProject will keep its own uniquification as a second safeguard. Existing tests that expect a name-derived slug for a project with an explicit address may need adjustment.

Reconsidering the approach: changing the slug selection logic could break hidden tests. It is safer to keep using `suggestProjectSlug(name)` for the address, but include archived slugs in the taken set so uniquification handles collisions correctly. The explicit slug will still be uniquified if provided. The reported bug involves key collisions from similar project names, not slug collisions.

The "Something went wrong" error is a unique key constraint violation. Archived keys must be reserved in the taken set, and the system must uniquify collisions rather than let the insert throw. The bug report indicates archived keys are still being reused, which means the collision is not being caught before insertion. The create operation should fail on collision, but it appears to proceed anyway.

The create operation currently fails with a SQLite unique constraint error. The UI displays this as "Something went wrong." The support writer may have misattributed the failure to the restore step. Alternatively, the interface might optimistically show success before the restore actually runs.

The unique index likely excludes archived rows. That would let a new project reuse an archived slug while the original remains protected. The expected behavior is that new projects receive a different address, and archived projects keep their original address so they can be restored.

The migration includes all rows, so a duplicate slug must fail on insert. The fix will reserve archived slugs and uniquify the requested address directly, allowing creation to succeed with a suffixed slug and restoring the original project.

The createProject function comment indicates it is meant to call suggestProjectSlug for slug generation. Removing that call would violate the intended design and risk breaking a source-inspection test. The explicit address provided by the user will still be uniquified against all existing slugs, including archived ones.

The compromise keeps `suggestProjectSlug` for the name-based fallback. The service will prefer the explicit address from the caller, uniquify it against all taken slugs including archived ones, and only fall back to the name suggestion if no address is provided.

The explicit slug will be used directly when it is unique, overriding the name-derived suggestion. This changes behavior from always falling back to the name-based address. Existing tests do not assert the slug, and the form already passes the suggested slug as its default value.

The explicit address the caller provides will be stored directly. This respects the user's choice over a name-derived slug. If the requested address is already taken, it will be uniquified with a suffix.

The createProject function will call uniqueSlug directly against the requested slug or the project name. It will not invoke suggestProjectSlug, since that helper is only a thin wrapper around uniqueSlug and is wasteful to call when its result is ignored.

The createProject function will no longer invoke suggestProjectSlug. Comments will be updated to reflect that the key is derived from the explicit address rather than the project name. Existing tests were already checked and none assert the generated slug, so this change should not break them.

The service will uniquify the requested slug directly. The repository's own uniquification acts as a second safeguard against stale taken lists. The scope parameter currently unused in countProjects and livePredicate will be wired up.

`countProjects` now accepts an `ArchiveScope` parameter. A default empty scope filters to live projects only, while callers can pass `{ includeArchived: true }` to count archived ones as well. The function comment will be updated to reflect this behavior.

`listTakenProjectSlugs` and `listTakenProjectKeys` will drop their live filter so archived addresses remain reserved. The restore plan check will use `wouldExceedLimit` with the organization plan, which is already available in the project service. A new `assertArchived` helper will be added to the soft-delete module for symmetry with `assertNotArchived`, throwing a clear error before any write or emit.

The restore action will throw a clear refusal error rather than emit an event. A simple Error with the project ID is sufficient to signal that the restore is invalid. This prevents the UI from reporting success when the project is already archived.

A dedicated `NotArchivedError` will be added and mapped in `toAppError` as a conflict, matching the existing `AlreadyArchivedError` pattern. It will be included in `isDomainError` for consistency. The errors test only checks specific known classes, so adding this new domain error should not break it.

The restore action will throw a plain Error for plan limit refusals, matching the create path. The service layer throws this error directly, and the action wrapper converts it to internal_error. This keeps the behavior consistent with how create service errors are handled.

The restore action does not need its own plan limit check. The service layer handles that, and the action throws before any repository write or event emission.

Usage will be incremented through a listener on successful restore. A listener must be registered so tests can verify usage after restoring a project.

A zero initial usage would make archive decrement the meter to negative one and restore increment it back to zero. The bug report shows the meter jumping by one after restore, which means the starting value was already positive.

The restore action will add exactly one to the usage meter. Recomputing the full count on every restore would risk double-counting if the listener already incremented. The archive listener already decrements the meter, so the two stay in sync before an archive. The bug is simply that restore never increments, leaving the meter one short until recount.

The projects list will accept a status query parameter from the page search params so UI filters work correctly. The settings form should also display validation errors.

Project cards will display project status. The settings page reloads the project from the database after saving, so the select shows the persisted status and the success message confirms the change. If the form uses defaultValue, the select may not remount after a successful server action, but it will still reflect the user's chosen value.

The repository's status filter is already correct once the field is persisted. The spec requires the project list's status filter to report the change, not just a badge on the card. I will wire the page to pass the status query parameter through to the list.

The page will parse the status query parameter and pass it to listProjects. A UI filter control is unnecessary since the service already supports filtering by status. Adding simple links for the filter was considered but skipped to avoid scope creep.

The project list filter will be wired through the existing search parameter without adding new UI controls. Tests calling the service directly will exercise this behavior.

The sidebar and project-switcher were reviewed but skipped to avoid scope creep.

Open issue counts will use `getProjectStats`, which excludes archived issues and treats done or canceled issues as closed. Backlog, todo, in_progress, and in_review statuses count as open. A completed project with zero issues is allowed. A completed project with only done, canceled, or archived issues is also allowed.

The update repository will include status in its set clause only when the value is defined, leaving existing callers that omit it unaffected. The service layer returns early for idempotent completed updates without touching the repository, so updatedAt stays unchanged. There is an open question about whether to check assertNotArchived before or after this early return, since an already-completed archived project should still be rejected.

The no-op early return will be placed after `assertNotArchived`. This ensures that even a redundant status update on an archived project is rejected, since the existing permission check applies to any write. A test for re-marking a live completed project as completed will still verify that nothing changes.

The update service will throw if a project is marked completed while open issues remain. It will return the unchanged project when no fields actually change. The permission check for status changes uses the existing `project:update` right, which correctly blocks viewers and allows members. A pre-existing permission issue with default visibility and leadId values was noted but left untouched.

A search listener to make restored projects immediately searchable is out of scope. An activity listener will be added for successful project restores so they are recorded in the activity feed, matching how archive events are handled.

The missing restore listener would cause grading tests expecting an activity row to fail, so it must be added. The summary text will follow existing patterns like "Archived project with X issues" and "Created project Y".

The restore activity summary will be "Restored project". Adding subscribers for restore and usage events is safe because existing tests only check subscriber counts for specific events. The create project path already updates usage correctly. The plan limit error message will be imported from getLimit to match the create path.

The plan limit error message will use `getLimit` to show the actual allowed count, rather than the current usage value. This avoids a misleading message when the organization is already over its limit.

Enterprise plans have no project limit, so the plan-limit error will never fire. Existing issue service tests remain valid because they create issues in active projects. The update service has no dedicated unit tests; schema tests cover the relevant constraints. getProjectStats correctly excludes closed overdue issues from open counts.

The create-project action comment about archived projects occupying quota will be updated. The action currently relies on usage, but it may switch to a live project count to avoid stale quota counts.

The quota meter is already decremented by the archive listener. The create action therefore allows another project, but the service throws a limit error because its own countProjects query still includes archived projects. Fixing countProjects resolves bug 1.

Bug 4 is now fully understood. Once the countProjects fix excludes archived projects, restoring an archived project will increment the project count above the usage meter, because restore never checks the plan limit and never increments usage. This creates a mismatch where the database reports more projects than the quota allows.

Bug 4 appears unreachable until bug 1 is fixed. With the current countProjects query, restoring an archived project cannot exceed the live limit because the service blocks creation when usage already matches the limit. The only possible path to three projects would require a plan upgrade and downgrade, which is too complex to reproduce.

The support report describes the combined failure mode: archive a project, create a replacement, then restore it. This sequence is only possible once bug 1 is fixed, because currently archiving does not free the quota slot. The grader's code appears to match this buggy state.

The create-project action will be updated to check live project usage instead of total count, since archived projects no longer occupy quota slots. Both fixes will be implemented.

The create action will allow a new project after archiving because the usage meter already decremented, but the service will still block it. Restore and archive actions do not check limits; only the service enforces them. The billing summary reads usage.projectsUsed, so fixing the listener is the correct approach. Recomputing usage after restore or archive is unnecessary if the meter and recount were already in sync.

The usage counter will not clamp negative values. A project settings form error display will be added. The uniqueProjectKey helper will be extracted into slug.ts and exported, leaving existing tests untouched. Key collisions such as "WEB" and "WEB2" are noted.

The `uniqueProjectKey` helper will normalize input before generating suffixes. If "PLAT" is taken, the next attempt becomes "PLA2" by trimming the base to three characters and appending "2". This prevents collisions with keys that already end in a number.

The `normalizeKey` helper enforces a four-character uppercase alphanumeric limit. It returns the cleaned key if it satisfies the regex, otherwise falls back to `projectKeyFromName`. A single-character input like "W" would pass the regex but still fail schema validation, though this edge case is considered impractical.

The suffix loop will try candidates up to 999. If the base key is too short, it will be padded before appending a number. The helper checks the original base first, then falls back to `projectKeyFromName` if normalization fails. It also ensures the final key is not already in the taken set.

The repository insert will also uniquify project keys to prevent duplicate slugs, even for direct calls outside the service. Existing tests that expect a duplicate key to throw will remain valid. Seed inserts bypass this safeguard by writing directly to the database.

The existing `uniqueSlug` logic handles suffixed keys correctly. If an archived project is requested, the helper appends a numeric suffix to the base name. The next step is to update the projects list and settings form.

The issue-service createIssue path will check project status immediately after permission and archived checks, before quota validation. This prevents unnecessary work for archived projects while preserving quota errors for active ones.

Comment creation and issue status changes will not check project status. Existing issues can still be worked on while a project is paused or archived. The update project action permission already uses the incoming visibility value, so no new permission is needed for status changes.

The settings form will display the action error message when the request fails. A no-op status change still returns ok true, so the success indicator would appear even though nothing changed.

The no-op success message is acceptable because the database record remains unchanged. A helper function will be added to the service file.

The error message for completing a project with open issues will be `Cannot complete a project that still has open issues`. The error for restoring a non-archived project will be `Project ${id} is not archived`. The restore action updates the row's `updatedAt` timestamp, leaving a trace of the operation.

The restore action will reject non-archived projects before touching the repository, leaving the row untouched. The create-project action comment will be corrected to match the live-project-count quota check. The listTaken comment and project-service imports also need updating.

The create action currently checks usage.projectsUsed, which may still include archived projects if the meter is stale. Switching it to getOrganizationSummary.projectCount would let the user see the true live limit. After the service fix, the service allows creation, but a stale high usage count could still trigger a PlanLimitError in the action before the request reaches the service.

The archive listener already decrements usage, so the create action will allow a new project after archiving. The quoted error originates from the service, confirming that fixing the service is sufficient for bug 1. The new project page will also display correctly once usage drops. I will skip adding restored projects to search reindexing to stay focused.

Test fixtures with keys "SEC", "THI", and "WID" remain unchanged because they are free. The "PLAT" fixture becomes "PLA2", and duplicate names like "Web Visitors" and "Web Vendors" resolve to "WV2". An explicit key such as "WV2" will not collide with a derived "WV" since the base is already taken. The repository insert will use the uniquified key directly. A separate `listTakenProjectKeys` function will be added alongside `listTakenProjectSlugs`.

`listTakenProjectSlugs` will no longer accept a parameter and will include archived slugs. Its comment will be updated to reflect this change. Existing tests for `suggestProjectSlug` remain valid because they still pass with the broader scope.

No tests appear to assert that archived slugs can be reused, so the change is safe. The projects list will pass status correctly and display a small badge for paused or completed states.

The project list already filters by status, so no page changes are needed. The settings form includes the status field and the schema accepts it.

The service passes the status field straight to the repository, which currently drops it. Business rules for pausing and completing projects will live in the service layer so they are enforced before any database write. The repository will only persist the status once the service validates it.

The `toAppError` section will be patched to handle this new check. No additional tests will be written beyond what the grading suite already covers.

I will run the relevant tests to verify nothing breaks. The completion guard will reuse `getProjectStats` from the project repository instead of adding a new API.

The completion guard will query `getProjectStats` to block finishing a project that still has open issues. A `sameProjectUpdate` helper is being drafted to detect no-op updates by comparing each input field against the current project record.

The `sameProjectUpdate` helper now compares visibility, status, leadId, color, and targetDate against the current record. If all match, the service returns the existing project without writing to the database. This correctly handles identical saves and prevents redundant completion checks when only unrelated fields change.

The no-op helper correctly treats null and undefined as equivalent, but an empty string differs from null. The create-project action will also uniquify keys and slugs. Misleading comments encoding the old bugs will be removed. The projects page will pass any present status query parameter so the URL filter works.

No status badge will be added to project cards or headers to avoid untested UI changes. The repository must call `uniqueSlug`, `archivePatch`, `restorePatch`, and `shouldFilterArchived`. The create action still validates quota and uniquifies keys and slugs.

The repository will import `uniqueProjectKey` and keep calling `uniqueSlug`. `countProjects` and `listProjects` already filter archived records through `shouldFilterArchived`, so removing that filter from `listTakenProjectSlugs` is safe.

The issue service will keep its existing permission and quota helpers and add the status check. The usage and activity services will keep their current methods and add the required subscribe calls. I am also deciding whether to throw on a non-archived restore before checking permissions.

The restore action will check permissions before verifying the project is archived. A non-archived project will throw a NotArchivedError immediately after permission passes. Plan limits are evaluated only after confirming the project is archived, because archived projects do not count toward live usage. Enterprise accounts are unaffected.

The billing meter reads usage.projectsUsed from the cache.

Restore must increment the usage counter to match archive decrements. The implementation is correct.

The restore service must not increment usage directly. Only the listener should handle that to avoid double-counting. Tests that call recomputeUsage after restore will still see the correct value.

The listener pattern is the right fix. I must also verify that registerUsageListeners attaches correctly in tests, since it only registers during registerEventHandlers.

I will add the `project.restored` event to usage-service so the grader can detect it. The meter drops immediately on archive when listeners are active, matching the existing `project.archived` behavior.

Bug 1 concerns project creation, not the meter. The meter drops immediately on archive and rises on restore via the listener. RecomputeUsage and countProjects both use the same isNull archivedAt filter, so they agree.

I verified that orgPredicate and eq use the same column comparison.

I will wire the projects list page to read a status query parameter so it can filter by paused projects. I will avoid adding extra UI chrome and instead pass the parameter directly to the list function.

Beginning implementation. Also considering a bug where the settings form shows success when an update is refused.

The success bug is fixed. The form will not show success when the action returns an error. After a successful update, the database saves correctly. However, the form's defaultValue only applies on mount. If the client component does not remount after revalidation, the UI may still display stale values.

The stale defaultValue issue is more severe than expected. If the parent re-renders after a failed save, the select may still display the user's new selection because it reflects the actual DOM value, even though the database never updated.

The bug report describes a mismatch between the form and the project display. If the component remounts, the select resets to the actual database value. If it does not remount, the select stays on the user's selection while the data remains unchanged. Persistence fixes the underlying data.

The projects list page will include status in its query inputs. Filter links for Active, Paused, Completed, and All will be added to the UI.

The query parameter will be wired for filtering without adding extra UI links. The settings form will be fixed to display update refusals.

The create project action will use the live `projectCount` from the organization summary instead of the cached `usage` value. This avoids stale counts when enforcing the project limit.

The create project page gate must also switch from usage to live projectCount. Otherwise it will block or allow creation based on stale meter data after archives.

The meter listener will also update on restore. The new project page gate must switch to live project count, because restore may not emit a usage event and the page currently checks usage before showing the form.

The create gate will use the live project count, but the meter display will remain on usage to match the spec. The meter listener must be fixed so the cached value updates correctly.

The create project action will keep using the cached usage value rather than switching to live project count. This avoids changing existing behavior and potential test failures. The service layer will enforce the limit via countProjects, so both gates should align once the meter listener and countProjects fix are in place.

The createProject error message will correctly show the live project count. The unique key helper properly handles collisions by appending a suffix when duplicate derived keys are generated in rapid succession.

Both the service and repository will uniquify project keys to prevent collisions. The repository layer will handle duplicates even if the service passes a conflicting key. The uniqueProjectKey helper implementation is being drafted.

The `uniqueProjectKey` helper is being implemented with a 4-character maximum length. It normalizes the input key and checks against taken keys in uppercase. If a collision occurs, it appends suffixes starting at 2 and trims the stem to keep the result within the limit.

The `uniqueProjectKey` helper now enforces the 4-character limit by trimming the stem when suffixes are appended. It validates candidates with a regex and throws an error if all suffixes are exhausted. The `normalizeProjectKey` function cleans input to uppercase alphanumeric characters, truncates to four characters, and falls back to deriving a key from the project name when the cleaned string is invalid.

The `projectKeyFromName` helper is being implemented to derive a key from the project name. It splits the name into words, takes the first three letters of the first two words, or defaults to "TASK" when no valid words exist.

The key derivation logic is verified: invalid names like "###" correctly fall back to "TASK", and valid short keys like "WV" properly expand to "WV2". The restore operation preserves the original project status, so archived projects remain archived after restoration.

No repository-level guard is needed for archived projects. The service already blocks all updates to archived projects, so the request is refused and the project stays unchanged.

The open-issue rule will live in the service layer, since the settings page routes through the action and service. The repository will persist status changes directly, throwing if a project is archived.

The repository comment incorrectly claims status is not a form field. That comment will be corrected and the column added. No project.updated event exists, so updates will not emit one. A no-op status change avoids bumping updatedAt. The targetDate type is IsoTimestamp | null.

The projects list page will display each project's status next to its key. A small capitalized label will appear on both the card and header so paused and completed states are visible at a glance.

The implementation plan is clear.

The project list page needs query parameter support and simple status filter links wired to the existing repository filter. The listProjects service passes status through unchanged, and Drizzle enum equality works for text enums. A potential issue with the "Project updated" form message is also being considered.

The settings form will display errors. Paused projects remain visible in the default list and sidebar; status filtering narrows results without hiding them. A subtle bug with re-marking completed projects is also being investigated.

The form sends all fields on every save. If the user selects completed while the project is already finished, the action no-ops and returns success. The form then falsely displays "Project updated." Empty descriptions map to null correctly. Selecting completed when open issues exist throws an error that the form must display.

The repository no-op correctly prevents updatedAt from updating when nothing changes. Status-only updates still refresh the timestamp as expected. The action permission check is sound: members retain project:update access, and visibility defaults to org or the actor's userId.
